alt: A grey clay bust of a human man with swept-back hair, seen from three-quarter view, standing on a round turned pedestal base.
caption: The default bust in grey clay on its printable base. The shoulders are cut flat and the bust stands on a turned pedestal.

alt: A grey clay bust of a bearded dwarf with a ring of dreadlocks and his mouth slightly open.
caption: A dwarf with dreadlocks, a full beard and the jaw slightly open: the model that was printed first.

alt: A grey clay bust of a half-orc with a mohawk, a scowl, the mouth open and a small tusk showing.
caption: A half-orc with the jaw open and snarling: teeth, a tongue and a tusk that turns with the jaw.

alt: A grey clay bust of a tiefling with a swept hairstyle and curled ram horns.
caption: A tiefling with ram horns. Horns come from a handful of generated shapes and are joined to the skull.

alt: A grey clay bust of a bearded man with two long braids hanging beside his face.
caption: Braids and a short beard. Hair and beards are carved shells with their strands cut in.

alt: Two side sections of a bust through the middle of the face. On the left the underside of the chin is marked red as a flat overhang; on the right a straight sloping wedge joins the chin to the neck and the red is gone.
caption: Why the throat gusset exists: without it the chin's flat underside hangs about 9 mm over air and needs supports; with it the underside is a 45 degree slope that prints on its own.
